title: Wall drawing
rule: Drawn in charcoal on the plaster of the station wall, the cupboard and the SERVICE door being real parts of that wall.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: the whole page is one stretch of office wall: lime plaster made from the teuf-teuf rock relief (charcoal99.wall, Cueva de las manos, CC BY-SA 3.0) at a paler level with HANDMADE lime-wash unevenness, two smoothed patches, four cracks with a light lip, nail holes and the clean ghost of a notice that once hung there; a card skirting board with moulding and a scrubbed board floor below it

three REAL parts of that wall, built as grey charcoal cards with their own drop shadows (charcoal99.pin_up): the wall clock hanging on its nail at 4:10 (b1m2 clock), the office cupboard standing against the wall (door on the left jamb; inside, the ANRC 1922 key cutout cut as a pale card on its hook with a SERVICE tag card), and the SERVICE door in its card architrave with a SERVICE card; a stick of charcoal (card) lies on the skirting ledge with its dust

everything else DRAWN on the plaster in charcoal (HANDMADE): six rough frames, the agent and the stranger as outlines of the b1m2 figure model with hatching and finger smudge, each nearer shape erasing the lines behind it; desk, memo slip, ticket window lettered TICKET OFFICE; captions and the four canon lines in the shared pen hand rubbed as charcoal; balloons rag-cleaned on the plaster with charcoal outlines

the drawing uses the real things: in frame 4 the drawn agent looks up (a drawn arrow) at the real clock, captioned 'a real one, on its nail'; a long charcoal arrow runs from frame 5 down the wall to the real cupboard; frame 6 is drawn round the real cupboard and the real SERVICE door, the drawn agent standing before the open cupboard

events.E0: frame 1: drawn desk and memo slip, the agent getting up; frame 2: walking 'toward the cupboard'
events.E1: frame 3: drawn ticket window, the lady; question balloon
events.E2: frame 4: the drawn agent looks up at the REAL clock (4:10); answer balloon
events.E3: frame 5: thanks balloon; 'She goes. He goes on to the cupboard, down there.' with an arrow to the real cupboard
events.E4: frame 6: the real cupboard open, the key card on its hook, SERVICE tag; caption
events.E5: frame 6: drawn agent, pencil to chin, forgetting balloon; the real SERVICE door closed; caption

beat: the story is drawn onto the wall frame by frame around the real things; the real cupboard door swings open on the wall before the last frame is drawn round it
beat_frames: b01: the bare wall: plaster, the real clock, the real closed cupboard, the real SERVICE door, the skirting
b04: frame 4 drawn under the real clock
b05: frame 5 and the arrow to the cupboard
b06: the real cupboard door half open
b07: frame 6 drawn round the open cupboard and the SERVICE door, no line yet
b08: the forgetting balloon written (= the page)

self_check.drawn_in_charcoal: frames, figures, desk, memo, window, lettering, balloons, arrows
self_check.check: A reader says the story is drawn on a wall: plaster texture, cracks, skirting and floor, real furniture standing in front of the drawing (perceptually judged from the full-size page by the maker)
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker

weaknesses: the plaster takes the charcoal99 greenish-sepia ramp, so it reads as an old distempered wall rather than fresh white lime
the caption '(a real one, on its nail)' explains the device instead of leaving it to the picture
the question balloon's tail crosses the drawn TICKET OFFICE board
the open cupboard leaf dips a little below the floor line toward the folio band
